catalog_quote: Ударение в агульском языке слабое динамическое и обычно падает на второй слог (муду́р 'козленок', къере́къел 'сорока') и при словоизменении не меняет позиции. Исключение составляют превербные и отрицательные формы глагола, в которых ударение перемещается на первый слог: уза́с 'доить' – отр. ф. ду́зас.

audit.recode_to: fixed-dominant (second syllable), or keep fixed-strict with a caution note — see reasoning; fix locator to 1999, pp. 399-408, sec. 2.1.2 p. 400
audit.reasoning: Quote: confirmed verbatim on the page scan of the official ILING e-copy downloaded now (book p. 400); year/pages should read 1999, 399-408 (StressTyp2's '2001, 398-408' carried into our the domain locator). Source quality: an encyclopedia sketch, but every fuller source I opened agrees on the default (weak dynamic stress on the 2nd syllable, stable under nominal inflection), so the second stress is safe. What the fuller sources add bears on the 'strict' flag, not the position: the deciding quote itself says 'обычно' and names systematic exceptions (preverbal and negative verb forms -> 1st syllable); Gasanova & Kaidov 2017 pp. 17-18 (held, unused) call Agul stress 'подвижное и разноместное', give initial stress on spatial preverbs (a large share of verb forms), disyllabic negatives, some loans and personal names, and lexical minimal pairs (атIа́с/а́тIас etc.); Borise 2018 sec. 5.1 (held) fil

sources.quote: "Stress in Agul is a weak dynamic stress and usually falls on the second syllable (mudúr 'kid (young goat)', qerékel 'magpie') and does not change position under inflection. The exception is preverbal and negative verb forms, in which stress moves to the first syllable: uzás 'to milk' – negative form dúzas." Talibov: "Stress usually falls on the second syllable, sometimes on the first." Meilanova: "Stress in the Lezgic languages is dynamic (expiratory), fixed predominantly on the second syllable
